content: In France, the social security system fully covers prenatal and postnatal care in public hospitals. Employed women are granted 16 weeks of maternity leave, with daily pay ranging from €9,29 ($10.94) to €84,90 ($100), based on prior income. Financially, the pregnancy and birth period is no tougher than usual: households already facing hardship remain so, and wealthier families stay comfortable. But when it comes to practical help for new mothers, there’s essentially nothing in place. Paternity leave is only 11 days, which doesn’t allow enough time for recovery after birth. New mothers are left to cope with relentless daily tasks while healing, and they must also secure childcare, even though state programs fall short, especially around Paris. Costs vary widely. In public daycare, lower-income families may pay about €1,000 ($1,177.59) per year, but there’s only one spot for every eight children. As a result, many turn to private options such as childminders or in-home care. Any other questions?
